 7 Tips for Caring for Plants during the Rainy Season to Stay Healthy 
 29 Oktober 2026, 01:27 | Editorial Team 
 MS Hadi 
 Reporter 
 Tim VOI 
 Editor 
 Illustration (Magnific/@muhammad.abdullah) 
 Share:
 YOGYAKARTA - The rainy season is good news for plants that need water supplies to grow after a long drought. However, if it rains almost every day, you need to pay more attention so that the collection of plants at home does not rot and die. The following will discuss a number of tips for caring for plants to stay healthy during the rainy season.
7 Tips for Caring for Plants during the Rainy Season Rain helps maintain soil moisture, but if the water flow is excessive it can make it difficult for the roots to get oxygen. In addition, the roots can also rot and fungal diseases can appear. Reported from Haddonstone, here are some simple steps that can be taken to keep the soil, roots, and leaves healthy during the rainy season.
Check Soil Moisture before Watering Your habit of watering plants every morning needs to be adjusted during the rainy season. Before taking the sprinkler, first check the soil condition by touching the surface with your fingers.
 If the soil is still wet, delay watering until the moisture is reduced according to the needs of the plant. This helps prevent water from accumulating around the roots, especially in potted plants that are outdoors.
Make sure the Pot has Good Drainage The drainage hole at the bottom of the pot serves to drain excess water so that it does not stagnate in the planting container. Without this channel, the roots can continue to be submerged and risk rotting.
 Make sure the drainage hole is not clogged by soil, roots, or dirt carried by rainwater. Clean the channel or you can move the plant to a pot with adequate drainage.
Move Plants that are Vulnerable to Heavy Rain Not all plants have the same water and weather resistance needs. Some ornamental plants are more easily damaged when they are constantly showered with rain, especially when the planting container is easy to hold water.
 The solution, move the plant to the roof terrace or other place that still gets light and air circulation. That way, the plant is spared from the rain and still gets the lighting it needs.
Cut the Leaves and Stems that are Damaged Heavy rain accompanied by strong winds can make leaves torn, broken stems, or parts of the plant drooping. After the weather improves, take the time to check the condition of the plants, whether there are parts that are damaged.
 Cut or remove broken, rotting, or diseased parts. This can reduce the parts that can potentially become a breeding ground for fungal problems.
Give Support to Plants that are Easily Robbed Tall-stemmed plants and vines are more prone to collapse when exposed to heavy rain. Meanwhile, the stems of plants that continue to be in a position to stick to the wet soil are at risk of rotting.
 The solution is to put a support stick and tie the plant stem loosely so that it stays upright without hindering its growth. Likewise, if there are small trees that seem to shake after the rain, you can water them until the roots grip the ground firmly again.
Maintain Air Circulation Around the Plants If the plants are placed too close together, the leaves can be difficult to dry after being exposed to rain. If it is left damp, the plants are more susceptible to fungi that can damage the leaves and stems.
 You can arrange for there to be a distance between one pot and another so that the air movement flows smoothly to the gaps between the plants. If there are plants in a narrow and stuffy corner, move them to a more open place so that the plants are not constantly damp.
Replace the Planting Pot if it is Too Wet If the plants show signs of excess water, such as yellowing leaves or rotting stems, it could be because of the planting container. You can consider replacing it with a new container that has good drainage.
 Do the transfer carefully so that the roots that are still healthy are not damaged. Place the plants that have been moved to the new container in a sheltered location for a while until their growth returns to normal.
 Those are some tips for caring for plants during the rainy season. By following the above care steps, your plants will stay healthy until the weather is sunny again.
